Archetypes

Feats you take here save onto the Character Builder character, in this browser apart from your D&D characters (💾 back up everything).
Archetypes, feats, and the archetype rules are from Pathfinder Player Core and Player Core 2 by Paizo Inc.; the Free Archetype variant is from Pathfinder GM Core. Used under the ORC License.

How archetypes work in Pathfinder 2e

An archetype is a theme you add on top of your class: a medic, a scout, a pirate, or a slice of another class. You start one with its dedication feat, taken in a class feat slot, usually from level 2. After that, the archetype's other feats can fill your class feat slots too, and archetype feats with the skill trait can fill skill feat slots.

The two-feat rule

Once you take a dedication, you can't take another one until you've taken two other feats from that archetype. Then you're free to start a second, and the same rule applies to it. The helper counts this for you and warns when a dedication comes too soon.

Multiclass archetypes

Each class has a multiclass archetype (Wizard Dedication, Fighter Dedication, and so on) that gives a piece of that class: some training, a class feature, and feats like Basic Arcana or Basic Wizard Spellcasting. Their dedications need every listed attribute at +2, and you can't take your own class's multiclass dedication.

Free Archetype

Free Archetype is a popular variant rule in GM Core: every character gets an extra class feat at 2nd level and every even level after, and it can only hold an archetype feat. Turn it on for a character (with your GM's say-so) and those slots show up here and in the Character Builder.

Works with

Build the character in the Character Builder and pick them here; the feats you take show up on the builder's sheet. A spellcasting archetype's spells go in the Spell Planner by hand for now.
